about: Every message Aaron typed or dictated in this session on Terra (the PC), copied verbatim from its log on 25 September 2026. Only his words. Taken from both places the log keeps them - the queued record of every message he sends and the plain user records - each message kept once at its earliest time. Messages he sent while Claude was still working sit in time order with the rest and are not marked apart, because a queued record alone does not show that. System text, tool output, skill instructions, task notifications, cross-session messages, compaction summaries and anything the studio wrote are excluded, as are the helper agents' logs beside this one.
title: Manifest Disunity design wiki

messages.text:
# The wiki designer's brief

**Paste this into a new Claude Code session started in this project folder.** This session builds
the generated design wiki. It is not an ideation session and not a programming session — it borrows
permissions from both and holds neither in full. Read the scope below before you touch anything.

Keep this file up to date as the wiki's shape changes.

---

You are building a wiki for **Manifest Disunity**, a browser strategy game Aaron is designing.
Aaron is a filmmaker and project manager, not a programmer — he cannot read code and does not want
to. Write every page for him: what a thing does and what governs it, in plain language, the way
`DESIGN.md` and the ideation documents already do. A future programmer reading the same page does
not need code-speak — they need the claim and exactly where it was decided.

## Why this exists

Three rounds of ideation — secession, conquest, politics — are done: 135 rulings, organized in
documents by *when* each was decided. Right shape for making the call, wrong shape for looking one
up. Aaron already hit the case where one fact lived in four places at once. Read `docs/FUTURE-IDEAS.md`
F24 before anything else — it is this idea's own charter and the source of the one rule below.

## The one hard rule

**Generated, not hand-written.** Four more rounds (economy, diplomacy, events, and the frame above
all of them) are still coming. A wiki someone typed by hand becomes a fifth place a fact can live and
the first one to go stale. Build something you can re-run after every future round closes, not a
one-time document. That likely means an actual script — see "Where this lives" below.

## Who it's for, and both get the same pages

1. **Aaron**, mid-conversation, pulling up "what are the rules for X" fast, and wanting to *see* how
   systems connect — including where they don't.
2. **Future programmers** — whoever runs architecture, planning and build once all seven rounds
   close — who need what's decided organized by system, not by date, with every claim citing the
   ruling that actually made it true.

**Not this wiki's job: playtesters.** Aaron didn't ask for that audience here, and F24 flagged a
playtester version as a separate, harder pass (it would have to hide anything about how the AI
decides). Don't build toward it.

## What a page is

One note per **nation**, per **movement**, per **mechanic** (federation, martial law, referendum,
vassal, union, and so on), per **ideology** (the ten board positions). Every claim on a page cites
the ruling or `DECISIONS.md` entry that made it true and links to it — never restate a rule as new
prose without pointing at where it was actually decided. If you can't find where a claim comes from,
that's a finding: write it down, don't invent a source.

**Point the vault at the real documents, not copies of them.** Don't duplicate ruling text into the
wiki pages. Open the vault on the project's `docs/` folder (plus `DESIGN.md` and `DECISIONS.md` at
the root) so a wiki page can link straight to a heading inside `politics-ideation.md` itself — one
copy of every fact, ever. The wiki you're building is the new layer of index pages that link *into*
that material, living in `docs/wiki/`.

## Tags are the actual deliverable, not decoration

Aaron wants to see how systems interact, including which pieces touch nothing else — that only shows
up if tagging is structured, not free text. Use a faceted scheme:

- `#nation/<name>`, `#movement/<name>`, `#ideology/<name>`
- `#system/secession`, `#system/conquest`, `#system/politics`, `#system/economy`,
  `#system/diplomacy`, `#system/events`
- `#mechanic/<name>` — federation, martial-law, referendum, union, vassal, etc.
- `#round/1`, `#round/2`, `#round/3` — provenance

Every page also gets an **"Interacts with"** section: `[[links]]` to other pages, each with a short
clause saying *why* — not a bare list. ("[[Federation]] — joining one replaces this movement's demand
with a vote, ruling 33.") A page with nothing pointing at it and nothing in its own "Interacts with"
section is precisely the finding Aaron is asking this exercise to surface. Don't build a separate
mechanism to detect that — consistent tagging and linking makes Obsidian's own graph and tag panes
show it for free.

## What it's built from

`docs/design/secession-ideation.md`, `conquest-ideation.md`, `politics-ideation.md`; the
`DECISIONS.md` entries tied to those three rounds (they run roughly 7–11 September 2026 — confirm
the exact ids by reading the file, don't trust a range written here); the Movement Register; and
whatever data files hold the real nation and movement ids.

**Before any page can be trusted:** match every prose name in the rulings to its real id in the data.
The ids exist; the documents use names. Where a match isn't certain, write that down instead of
guessing.

## Where this lives, and what you may touch

**Create and edit freely:**
- `docs/wiki/` — the vault's new layer. Your output.
- A generator script under `build/`, next to the map and economy bakers already there — same kind
  of job, and it's how this stays regenerable instead of hand-maintained.
- `docs/FUTURE-IDEAS.md` — update F24 once this exists: what got built, and that the audience
  question is answered (Aaron and programmers, not playtesters).

**Read but never edit:**
- Every ideation document (`docs/design/*-ideation.md`). This wiki reports what they say. It is
  never where a new ruling happens.
- `DESIGN.md`, `data/`, `docs/spec/`.

**Never touch:**
- Any game code — `js/`, `css/`, `tests/`, `index.html`, `dev.html`, `server.py`.

## How I want you to work

Push back if something doesn't fit — say so and why. Give recommendations, not menus. Ask questions
one at a time: list them, ask the first, wait for the answer before the next. Never publish a number
you haven't checked against the actual file.

## Prove it before calling it done

Open the page for the **Sagebrush Rebellion**. It should show its position (Anarcho-Capitalism,
ruling 41's re-map), its growth cap (0.45, also ruling 41), and link out to whatever page explains
what crossing that cap does. If that chain works without reading any ideation document directly,
the wiki works. If it doesn't, that's the bug to fix before adding more pages.

Leave a short `README.md` in `docs/wiki/` saying how to re-run the generator — the next person to
need that is whoever closes round 4.

After you read through this ask me any questions you have and then give me a rundown of you plan of operations on this.

   2. how it works in the game

2. Allow me to see visually (with obsidians node graph feature) how everything in the game interacts with other systems
